mainTopic: Why a ruin is forbidden for three reasons, the number of watches in the night, and the stories of דוד rising at midnight.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives three reasons not to enter a חורבה (ruin): חשד (suspicion), מפולת (collapse) and מזיקין (demons). The גמרא shows that each reason is needed, by finding a case where only that one applies. Then a new ברייתא brings an argument: רבי says the night has four watches, and רבי נתן says three. Each side brings פסוקים and explains away the other side's proof, many of them about דוד rising at midnight. Along the way comes a law in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי about what one may say in front of a dead person. The גמרא then asks how דוד could rise at midnight if a פסוק says he rose at נשף, and רבא explains that נשף can mean either evening or morning. Finally, the גמרא asks how דוד knew the exact moment of midnight when even משה did not. It answers with the story of the כנור over his bed, and how דוד's advisers prepared for war.

steps.title: Suspicion is needed for a new ruin
steps.stepSummary: The reason of חשד is needed for a new, sturdy ruin, where there is no fear of collapse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a new ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it asked just before: why give the reason חשד when מפולת already covers it? The answer is that a new ruin will not collapse, so only חשד can forbid going into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason מפולת only works for an old, shaky ruin. A newly ruined building is still solid, so there is no collapse danger. Without the reason חשד, we would think a new ruin is allowed, so the ברייתא needs to give it.

keyTerms.meaning: New. Here, a ruin that was only recently destroyed and is still sturdy.
A ruin, an abandoned broken building
Suspicion. People may think he went in to meet a woman privately.

phrases.english: In a new one.
phrases.notes: He means a new ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question (just before this text) of why חשד is needed when מפולת is enough.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: חשד is needed for a situation where מפולת does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מפולת already forbids entering, the reason חשד seems extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a new, sturdy ruin there is no מפולת, so only חשד forbids it.

steps.title: Why not just use the danger of demons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: even in a new ruin, the reason מזיקין should be enough, so why is חשד needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him derive it because of demons!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Even if a new ruin won't fall, the ruin is still a place of מזיקין, so why do we need חשד?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer only removed the reason מפולת. The reason מזיקין still seems to apply to every ruin, new or old. So חשד again looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it (from another reason). A challenge that something is already covered.
Harmful spirits or demons, believed to live in ruins

phrases.english: But let him derive it because of demons?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 1 by pointing to the third reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חשד is needed for a new ruin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A new ruin still has מזיקין, so the reason חשד adds nothing.

steps.title: Two people entering together
steps.stepSummary: The case is when two people go in together. מזיקין only harm someone who is alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about two people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חשד is needed when two people go into the ruin together. מזיקין don't threaten a pair, so only חשד is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger of מזיקין is a danger to a person who is alone. Once two people go in, that reason falls away. Now the case has neither מפולת (a new ruin) nor מזיקין (two people).

phrases.english: With two.
phrases.notes: He means two people going in together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case further to two people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every ruin is forbidden because of מזיקין.
steps.terutzMaskana: When two go in, there are no מזיקין, so חשד is needed.

steps.title: With two people there is no suspicion either
steps.stepSummary: If two go in together, there should be no חשד either, since people don't suspect two men alone with a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is two people, then there is no suspicion either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If two people are together, nobody would suspect them of meeting a woman, so the reason חשד also disappears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer "two people" removed מזיקין, but it seems to remove חשד too. The rule is that two men may be alone with a woman, so normally there is no suspicion. Then the case has no reason left at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Being alone with a woman. Two men together do not count as יחוד.

phrases.english: If it is with two,
there is no suspicion either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is two people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same fact that removes מזיקין (two people) also removes חשד, so חשד can't be the reason for this case.

steps.title: Two people known to be immoral
steps.stepSummary: The case is two people who are known to be פריצים (immoral). Even two such people are suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about two people who are immoral.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is two people with a bad reputation. People would suspect even the two of them, so חשד still applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two men together usually remove suspicion only because they keep each other in check. If both are known to be immoral, that doesn't work, so there is still חשד. Now we have a full case that only חשד forbids: a new ruin (no מפולת), two people (no מזיקין), who are פריצים (so there is חשד).

keyTerms.meaning: Immoral people, people known to be loose in their behavior

steps.whatToRemember: חשד is needed for a new ruin entered by two פריצים. There is no collapse, no demons, but there is still suspicion.

phrases.english: With two who are immoral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 and finishes the explanation of why חשד is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case even more, to immoral people
steps.terutzMaskana: Two immoral people do raise suspicion, so חשד is needed for them.

steps.title: Why is the danger of collapse needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks about the second reason: why mention מפולת, if חשד and מזיקין already forbid entering?
steps.simpleTranslation: "Because of collapse": but let him derive it from suspicion and demons!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next reason in the ברייתא, מפולת. It asks why it is needed when חשד and מזיקין already cover it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that חשד has been shown to be needed, the גמרא checks the reason מפולת the same way. It looks like any ruin is already forbidden by חשד or by מזיקין. So the גמרא must find a case where only collapse applies.

phrases.english: "Because of collapse":
but let him derive it because of suspicion and demons!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי הַמַּפּוֹלֶת וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם חֲשָׁד וּמַזִּיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with חשד, opens a new check of the second reason, מפולת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חשד and מזיקין already forbid entering a ruin, so the reason מפולת seems extra.

steps.title: Collapse is needed when two decent people enter together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מפולת is needed in a case of two כשרים entering together. There is no חשד and no מזיקין there, but the ruin could still fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is two decent people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6 by giving a case where only the danger of collapse applies: two decent people go into the ruin together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people means מזיקין are not a worry, since they only harm someone alone. Decent people means there is no חשד. That leaves מפולת as the only reason, so it is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Decent, upstanding people (the opposite of פְּרִיצֵי)
With two people, two going in together

phrases.english: With two people, and decent ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by finding a case where only מפולת applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a specific case where the other two reasons drop away
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חשד and מזיקין already forbid entering, מפולת seemed extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: With two decent people, only מפולת remains, so that reason is needed.

steps.title: Why mention demons if suspicion and collapse are enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now questions the third reason, מזיקין: חשד and מפולת should already be enough to forbid entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Because of demons": derive the rule from suspicion and collapse instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third reason in the ברייתא, מזיקין, and asks why it is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge already raised against חשד and מפולת. If the other two reasons always apply, then מזיקין adds nothing new. The גמרא wants a case where only מזיקין would apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it come out from (another reason): why not just use the other reason?

phrases.english: "Because of demons":
Let it be derived from suspicion and collapse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending מפולת, the גמרא runs the same test on the third reason, מזיקין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חשד and מפולת already forbid entering, then מזיקין seems to be an unneeded extra reason.

steps.title: A new ruin with two decent people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a case where only מזיקין applies: a new ruin (no מפולת) entered by two decent people (no חשד).
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a new ruin, with two decent people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer by building a case that removes both the collapse worry and the suspicion worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new ruin is not likely to fall, so there is no מפולת. Two decent people means there is no חשד. The idea is that only מזיקין would then be left.

keyTerms.meaning: New (a ruin that only recently became a ruin and is still strong)

phrases.english: In a new ruin,
and with two decent people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by combining two conditions: a new ruin and two decent people.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a specific case to isolate one reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מזיקין seemed unneeded because חשד and מפולת always apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a new ruin with two decent people, supposedly only מזיקין is left.

steps.title: With two people there are no demons either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer: if two people go in, there is no danger of מזיקין either, so this case has no reason at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are two people, there are no demons either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer from step 9: the 'two people' condition that removed suspicion also removes the demons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From step 3 we know מזיקין only harm someone who is alone. So in the case of step 9, none of the three reasons applies, and we still have no case where only מזיקין matters. The question stays open for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: There is also none: this one doesn't apply either

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think step 9 settled things. The גמרא shows that the answer in step 9 fails, because 'two people' cancels מזיקין too.

phrases.english: If it is with two people,
there are no demons either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9 using the rule from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case proposed in step 9 (new ruin, two decent people)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two people together are not harmed by מזיקין, so this case removes all three reasons and does not isolate מזיקין.

steps.title: In a place known for demons, even two must worry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question of step 10. Usually two people are safe from מזיקין, but in a place where מזיקין are known to be, even two are in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: In their place, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge that two people have nothing to fear from מזיקין. It says that in a place where מזיקין live, we worry even about two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the case of two people in a new ruin has no reason at all, because two people are safe from מזיקין. The answer limits that rule: being two only protects you in an ordinary place. In a place where מזיקין are known to be found, even two people are at risk, so the reason of מזיקין is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: In their place: a place where מזיקין are known to be
We are concerned / we worry about it

phrases.english: In their place, we are concerned.
phrases.notes: 'Their place' means a spot where the מזיקין are known to be found. There, being two does not protect you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and saves the case from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule that two people are safe from מזיקין to ordinary places.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two people are never in danger from מזיקין, so a new ruin entered by two has no reason to forbid it.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a place known to be a haunt of מזיקין, even two people are in danger, so מזיקין is a needed reason.

steps.title: Another answer: one person in a new ruin out in the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second answer. The case is one person entering a new ruin in an open field. There is no חשד and no מפולת, but there is still danger from מזיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: Really it is talking about one person, in a new ruin that stands in a field. There, there is no חשד, because a woman is not usually found in a field. But there is still the reason of מזיקין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different case where only מזיקין applies: one person in a new ruin out in a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer goes back to one person, so the danger of מזיקין is clear. The ruin is new, so it will not fall (no מפולת). It is out in the field where women are not around, so nobody will suspect him (no חשד). That leaves only מזיקין, which proves that reason is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: the גמרא is offering another answer
Really / actually: the case is in fact this
A new ruin, which will not collapse soon

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. The first answer keeps the case of two people. This second answer switches to one person and moves the ruin out to a field to remove חשד.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three reasons (חשד, מפולת, מזיקין) has a case where it is the only reason, so all three are needed.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Really it is about one person,
and in a new ruin that stands in a field,
for there, the reason of suspicion does not apply,
since a woman is not usually found in a field,
but the reason of demons does apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the challenge of steps 8 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new case where only מזיקין applies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no case where מזיקין is the only reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: One person in a new ruin in a field: no מפולת, no חשד, only מזיקין.

steps.title: How many watches does the night have: four or three?
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: רבי says the night has four watches. רבי נתן says it has three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The night has four watches; these are the words of רבי. רבי נתן says: three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with an argument about how many watches (parts) the night is split into.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic, connected to the משנה's time 'until the end of the first watch'. רבי splits the night into four parts. רבי נתן splits it into three. The next steps look at the source for this argument.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The night has four watches,
these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: three.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבַּע מִשְׁמָרוֹת הָוֵי הַלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after finishing the ruin discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: the night has four watches. רבי נתן: three watches.

steps.title: What is רבי נתן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי נתן's view of three watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי נתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי נתן gets the idea that the night has three watches. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The גמרא simply wants to know the source. The answer will be a פסוק.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Natan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי נתן's opinion in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for saying the night has three watches.

steps.title: The פסוק about גדעון and the 'middle watch'
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן's source is the פסוק saying גדעון came at 'the start of the middle watch'. A ברייתא explains that 'middle' means one before it and one after it, so there are three watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And גדעון and the hundred men with him came to the edge of the camp at the start of the middle watch.' It was taught: 'Middle' only means something that has one before it and one after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a פסוק that talks about 'the middle watch'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'middle' means there is exactly one watch before it and one after it. That makes three watches in total. This is the proof for רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: A watch (part of the night), the word used in the פסוק

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came
phrases.notes: שופטים 7:19

phrases.english: to the edge of the camp
at the start of the middle watch."
It was taught:
"Middle" only means
one that has one before it and one after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's view that the night has three watches.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 7:19, 'the middle watch', with a ברייתא explaining 'middle' as one before and one after.

steps.title: How רבי reads 'middle'
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains the פסוק differently: 'middle' means one of the two middle watches out of four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, what does he do with 'middle'? It means one of the middle ones among the middle watches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי, who holds four watches, explains the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With four watches, there are two in the middle (the second and the third). רבי says the פסוק's 'middle watch' means one of those two. So the פסוק does not prove there are only three.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי and רבי נתן accept the פסוק of 'the middle watch'. They only argue about whether 'middle' means the one middle of three, or one of the two middles of four.

phrases.english: And Rabbi, what does he say "middle" means?
One of the middle ones among the middle watches.
phrases.notes: With four watches, the 2nd and 3rd are both 'middle'. The פסוק means one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the proof of step 15 from רבי's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the night has only three watches. רבי accepts the פסוק itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Middle' does not have to mean the single middle of three. It can mean one of the two middle watches out of four.

steps.title: רבי נתן defends his reading of 'the middle watch'
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן rejects רבי's reading. The פסוק says just 'the middle' (תיכונה), not 'one of the middle ones', so there must be exactly one middle watch, which means three watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי נתן answer? Does the פסוק say 'the middle one of the middle ones'? It just says 'the middle'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן pushes back against רבי's explanation from Step 16 and defends his own proof that there are three watches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי read 'the middle watch' as one of two middle watches out of four. רבי נתן answers that the פסוק says simply 'the middle', which sounds like the one and only middle watch. Only one watch can be truly in the middle if the night has three watches.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle one out of several middle ones
Is it written...? (a way of saying the פסוק does not say that)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Natan, how does he answer?
Is it written "the middle one of the middle ones"?
"The middle" is what is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's rejection in Step 16 and puts back רבי נתן's proof from the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי's reading of 'the middle watch' as one of two middle watches.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording 'תיכונה' means a single middle watch, so it does not fit 'one of the middle ones'.

steps.title: What is רבי's source for four watches?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source supports רבי's view that the night has four watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for רבי's own positive source. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רבי has only defended himself against רבי נתן's proof from גדעון. Now the גמרא wants his own proof for four watches, just as it asked for רבי נתן's source in Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: Four watches, which is רבי's view

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי נתן's proof to looking for רבי's own source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows the night has four watches.

steps.title: Two פסוקים about דוד show four watches
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי puts two פסוקים together. דוד rose at midnight, and he also says his eyes came before the 'watches' (at least two). Both can be true only if the night has four watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: One פסוק says, 'At midnight I rise to thank You for Your righteous laws.' Another פסוק says, 'My eyes came before the watches.' How do they fit together? The night has four watches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by showing how two פסוקים in תהלים together prove four watches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says דוד got up at חצות לילה (midnight). The other says he woke up before 'watches', and the plural means at least two watches before morning. Midnight is exactly two watches before morning only if the night has four watches.

keyTerms.meaning: My eyes came first, meaning I woke up before
How can this be? (used to settle two sources that seem to clash)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key proof for four watches, and the rest of the section shows how רבי נתן can still read these same פסוקים his own way.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Ami said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One verse says:
"At midnight I rise to give thanks to You
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:62

phrases.english: for Your righteous laws,"
and another verse says:
"My eyes came before the watches"
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:148. 'Watches' is plural, so דוד woke up at least two watches before morning.

phrases.english: How can both be true?
The night has four watches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Midnight (from one פסוק) is two watches (from the other פסוק) before morning, so the night has four watches.

steps.title: רבי נתן counts until the kings wake up
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן follows רבי יהושע, who says kings wake at the third hour of the day. From midnight until then is six hours of night plus two of day, which equals two watches even if the night has only three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי נתן? He holds like רבי יהושע, as the משנה teaches: רבי יהושע says, until three hours, because kings usually get up at three hours. Six hours of night and two of day make two watches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי נתן handles רבי's proof from the פסוקים about דוד, while keeping three watches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי counted the 'watches' from midnight until morning. רבי נתן counts until the time kings get up, at the third hour of the day. In a three-watch night each watch is four hours, so six night hours plus two day hours is eight hours, which is two watches. דוד got up two watches before the other kings.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'watches' are counted until the kings wake up in the morning, not until dawn. That is why day hours are added to the count.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Natan, how does he explain these verses?
He holds like Rabbi Yehoshua.
As we learned in a mishnah: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
until three hours of the day,
because that is the way of kings
to get up at three hours.
Six hours of the night and two of the day
make two watches.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי נָתָן, סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי נתן's answer to רבי's proof in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the פסוק differently: the 'watches' are counted until the kings wake up, not until morning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Watches' meant two watches between midnight and morning, which would require four watches in the night.
steps.terutzMaskana: Midnight until the third hour of the day is eight hours, which is two four-hour watches, so three watches still works.

steps.title: A watch and a half can be called 'watches'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives another answer for רבי נתן: from midnight to morning is one and a half watches, and even that can be called 'watches' in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: One and a half watches are also called 'watches'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second, simpler way for רבי נתן to explain the פסוק about 'watches'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a three-watch night, midnight to morning is six hours, which is one and a half watches. רב אשי says the plural word 'watches' does not have to mean two full watches, so one and a half is enough. That way רבי נתן can count only until morning and still keep three watches.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי proves four watches from דוד rising at midnight, which he calls 'before the watches'. רבי נתן keeps three watches in one of two ways: count until the kings wake up (eight hours, two watches), or, like רב אשי, say a watch and a half is also called 'watches'.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A watch and a half also
are called "watches".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer for רבי נתן, different from the answer in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the plural word 'watches' more loosely.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural 'watches' must mean at least two full watches.
steps.terutzMaskana: One and a half watches (midnight to morning in a three-watch night) can also be called 'watches'.

steps.title: In front of the dead, speak only about the dead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that in front of a dead person, you may speak only about matters of the dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: In front of a dead person, you may only say things that concern the dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new teaching from רבי יהושע בן לוי, who was just quoted above. It sets a rule about what you may talk about when a dead person lies in front of you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new law, not part of the argument about the watches of the night. The rule is that the conversation around a dead person should be about the dead person. It should not be about other topics.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of the dead person (before he is buried)
Matters of the dead person, such as his burial and eulogy

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Zerika said, Rabbi Ami said,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One may not say, in front of the dead,
anything except matters of the dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an unrelated teaching from the same chain (רבי זריקא, in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי) that was quoted in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In front of a dead person, one speaks only about matters of the dead person.

steps.title: First version: the rule applies only to Torah talk
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא limits the rule. It forbids only words of Torah in front of the dead. Ordinary talk is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said: We only said this rule about words of Torah. But ordinary everyday matters are no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר כהנא explains how far the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי goes. In this version, the rule is narrow: it covers only words of Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning Torah in front of the dead looks like teasing him, because he can no longer learn. Everyday talk does not carry that message. So according to this version, everyday talk is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this about the following case (a phrase that limits a rule)
We have no problem with it; it is allowed

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:
We only said this about words of Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִילֵּי דְעָלְמָא לֵית לָן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but ordinary matters, we have no problem with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how far the rule from step 22 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only Torah talk is forbidden in front of the dead. Everyday talk is allowed.

steps.title: Second version: even Torah talk, and surely everyday talk
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבי אבא בר כהנא makes the rule broader. Even Torah talk is forbidden, so everyday talk is surely forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: רבי אבא בר כהנא said that the rule applies even to words of Torah, and all the more so to everyday matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of what רבי אבא בר כהנא said. This version turns the rule around and makes it wider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the starting point is that everyday talk is clearly not allowed. The new point is that even Torah, which we are commanded to speak about, is not allowed in front of the dead. If Torah is forbidden, then everyday talk is surely forbidden (כל שכן).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version, only Torah talk is forbidden. In the second version, everything except the dead person's matters is forbidden, Torah included.
steps.whatToRemember: Speaking in front of the dead: the first version forbids only Torah talk. The second version forbids even Torah talk, and all the more so everyday talk.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said
we said this [even] about words of Torah,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Read it as 'this applies even to words of Torah.'

phrases.english: and all the more so ordinary matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the limit from step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even Torah talk is forbidden in front of the dead, and all the more so everyday talk.

steps.title: Did דוד get up at midnight or in the evening?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that דוד got up at midnight. A פסוק says he got up at נשף, which seems to mean evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did דוד really get up at midnight? He got up in the evening! As it is written: 'I rose at נשף and cried out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to דוד המלך and asks a challenge. It quotes a פסוק that seems to say דוד got up in the evening, not at midnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned from 'חצות לילה אקום' that דוד got up at midnight. Now a different פסוק, 'קדמתי בנשף', seems to say he got up at נשף, which may mean evening. The two פסוקים seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A time word that can mean evening (and possibly other times)
I rose early; I got up before

phrases.english: And did David get up at midnight?
He got up from the evening!
As it is written: 'I rose at neshef and cried out,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:147

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the dead and goes back to the פסוקים about דוד from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that דוד got up at midnight ('חצות לילה אקום').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'קדמתי בנשף' says דוד got up at נשף, which seems to mean evening. That clashes with midnight.

steps.title: Proof that נשף means evening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a פסוק in משלי that נשף means evening, which makes the challenge stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this word נשף means evening? As it is written: 'In the נשף, in the evening of the day, in the blackness of night and darkness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its own challenge. It asks how we know נשף means evening, then brings a פסוק where נשף stands next to 'evening of the day.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 25 works only if נשף really means evening. The פסוק in משלי puts 'בנשף' right beside 'בערב יום', the evening of the day. That shows the two words mean the same time, so the question against midnight stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? How do we know?

phrases.english: And how do we know that this 'neshef' is evening?
As it is written: 'In the neshef, in the evening of the day,'
phrases.notes: משלי 7:9

phrases.english: in the blackness of night and darkness!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the challenge in step 25 by proving what נשף means.
steps.raayaObject: That the word נשף means evening.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 7:9, where 'בנשף' stands next to 'בערב יום'.

steps.title: Midnight never passed while דוד was asleep
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא explains that דוד was not claiming he always rose exactly at midnight. He was claiming that midnight never found him asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said in the name of רבי אחא: This is what דוד meant: 'Midnight never passed over me while I was asleep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the contradiction. דוד sometimes rose earlier, at נשף, but he was always awake by חצות at the latest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed 'I rise at midnight' means he rose exactly at midnight. רבי אחא reads it as a minimum instead: midnight never found him asleep. So rising at נשף on some nights fits too, because he was already awake before midnight.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant. It introduces a new way of reading a statement.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said,
Rabbi Acha said:
This is what (David) meant:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word דוד in round brackets. Either way, the speaker is דוד.

phrases.english: Never has there passed over me
midnight while I was asleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 25-26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: 'at midnight' marks the latest time, not the exact time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד always rose exactly at midnight, which clashes with rising at נשף
steps.terutzMaskana: Midnight was the latest he was ever asleep. Sometimes he rose earlier, at נשף.

steps.title: Dozing like a horse, then strong like a lion
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says that until midnight דוד only dozed lightly, like a horse, and after midnight he got up full of strength, like a lion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Until midnight he would doze like a horse. From then on, he would rise with the strength of a lion.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer. Before midnight דוד was half-awake and only dozed, which fits 'I rose at נשף.' At midnight he got up fully, which fits 'At midnight I rise.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A horse dozes but never falls into deep sleep. So from evening on, דוד was never really asleep, and both פסוקים are true: he was 'up' from נשף, and fully active from חצות.

keyTerms.meaning: From here on, from that point onward

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Until midnight
he would doze like a horse,
from then on
he would rise with strength like a lion.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר: עַד חֲצוֹת לַיְלָה הָיָה מִתְנַמְנֵם כְּסוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dividing the night: light dozing until midnight, full strength after it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rising at נשף and rising at חצות cannot both be true
steps.terutzMaskana: From נשף he only dozed, and at חצות he got up fully

steps.title: Torah until midnight, songs of praise after
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says דוד was awake the whole night. Until midnight he learned Torah, and after midnight he sang songs and praises.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Until midnight he would study words of Torah. From then on, he would engage in songs and praises.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer. דוד was up from נשף learning Torah, and at חצות he switched to singing praises to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two פסוקים describe two different activities. 'I rose at נשף' is about the start of his Torah learning. 'At midnight I rise to give thanks' is about the start of his praises.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers fit נשף and חצות together: (1) midnight never found דוד asleep; (2) he dozed until midnight, then rose like a lion; (3) he learned Torah until midnight, then sang praises.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Until midnight
he would study words of Torah,
from then on
in songs and praises.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: עַד חֲצוֹת לַיְלָה הָיָה עוֹסֵק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק describes a different activity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים describe the same act of getting up, so they clash
steps.terutzMaskana: He rose at נשף for Torah, and at חצות he began songs and praises

steps.title: Doesn't נשף mean morning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether נשף really means evening. A פסוק about דוד fighting seems to use נשף for morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does נשף really mean evening? Doesn't נשף mean morning? As it is written: 'And דוד struck them from the נשף until the evening of the next day.' Doesn't this mean from morning until night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the idea everyone has been relying on, that נשף means evening. It brings a פסוק where נשף seems to mean morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, נשף is paired with 'evening' as the endpoint. That suggests נשף is the opposite of evening, meaning morning. If so, step 26's proof that נשף means evening is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A time word whose meaning is being argued here: evening or morning
Doesn't it mean…? Used to push a proof.

phrases.english: And is 'neshef' evening?
But 'neshef' is morning!
As it is written:
'And David struck them from the neshef'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 30:17

phrases.english: 'until the evening of the next day.'
Doesn't it mean —
from morning until night?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֶשֶׁף אוּרְתָּא הוּא? הָא נֶשֶׁף צַפְרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of נשף, which the whole discussion has relied on
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נשף means evening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In שמואל א, נשף is the starting point and 'evening' is the endpoint, so נשף seems to mean morning

steps.title: No: from evening to evening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק in שמואל means דוד fought from one evening until the next evening. So נשף can still mean evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means from evening until the next evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. נשף in that פסוק can mean evening too: the battle ran from one evening to the evening of the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed נשף and 'evening' had to be opposite times. But the פסוק says 'the evening of the next day,' so the battle can run from one evening to the following evening. The proof that נשף means morning is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: No, used to reject a suggested reading

phrases.english: No,
from evening until evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 30
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from שמואל א that נשף means morning
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק can just as well mean from one evening to the next evening

steps.title: Why would the verse switch words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer from Step 31. If the פסוק meant evening to evening, it should have said 'נשף to נשף' or 'ערב to ערב,' not mixed the two words.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, the פסוק should have written 'from the נשף until the נשף' or 'from the evening until the evening'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. The פסוק uses two different words, and that does not fit the idea that both ends were the same time of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 said the פסוק meant one evening until the next evening. But the פסוק says 'from the נשף until the ערב.' If both ends were evening, why use two different words? Switching words suggests two different times, so נשף probably means morning here after all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
Let it write; the פסוק should have said
A time word in פסוקים; the debate is whether it means evening or morning

phrases.english: If so, let it write
phrases.notes: The פסוק being discussed is שמואל א 30:17, which says 'from the נשף until the evening of the next day.'

phrases.english: "from the neshef until the neshef"
or "from the evening until the evening"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the פסוק in שמואל means one evening until the next evening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses two different words, נשף and ערב. If both meant evening, it would have used the same word twice.

steps.title: רבא: נשף can mean two different times
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that there are two kinds of נשף. The word describes one part of the day passing into the next, so it can mean evening or morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: There are two times called נשף. The night passes and the day comes, and the day passes and the night comes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer. נשף does not mean only evening; it means any time when one part of the day gives way to the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We no longer need to choose between 'evening' and 'morning.' נשף names the moment of change, so it can be dawn or dusk. That explains the פסוק in שמואל, where it means morning, and still allows נשף to mean evening in other places.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given
Passes or moves away (as a verb)

steps.whatToRemember: נשף means a time of change. It can be the end of night (morning) or the end of day (evening).

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
There are two times called neshef
the night passes and the day comes,
phrases.notes: Here נשף is a verb meaning 'passes away.' That is why the same word fits both dawn and dusk.

phrases.english: the day passes and the night comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 32 with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the word so that it can carry both meanings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נשף must mean only evening or only morning
steps.terutzMaskana: נשף means any time when one part of the day passes into the next, so it can mean evening or morning

steps.title: How could דוד know exactly when midnight was?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how דוד could know the exact moment of midnight. Even משה רבינו did not know it, since he said 'about midnight.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And did דוד know exactly when midnight was? Even משה רבינו did not know, as it is written: 'About midnight I will go out into the midst of מצרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about דוד, who said he rose at midnight. It argues that knowing the exact moment of midnight is very hard, because even משה did not know it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's words 'at midnight I rise' sound like he knew the exact moment. But משה told פרעה 'about midnight,' which sounds like an estimate. If משה, the greatest נביא, could only estimate, how could דוד know exactly?

keyTerms.meaning: Midnight; literally, half of the night
Now; here it means 'look, even...' to build a strong comparison

phrases.english: And did David know
phrases.notes: This goes back to דוד's words in תהלים 119:62, 'At midnight I rise.'

phrases.english: when exactly midnight was?

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לָא הֲוָה יָדַע,
phrases.english: Now, even Moshe our teacher did not know,
as it is written: "About midnight
I will go out into the midst of Egypt."
phrases.notes: שמות 11:4

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדָוִד מִי הֲוָה יָדַע פַּלְגָא דְּלֵילְיָא אֵימַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of נשף and opens a new challenge about דוד knowing the time of midnight
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that דוד knew the exact moment of midnight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If משה רבינו could only say 'about midnight,' then the exact moment must be very hard to know. So how could דוד know it?

steps.title: Who said 'about midnight'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'about midnight' means. It rejects the idea that הקב"ה said it, because Heaven has no doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'about midnight' mean? If you say that הקב"ה told משה 'about midnight,' is there any doubt before Heaven?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the proof from Step 34 by asking whose uncertainty the word 'about' shows. It rules out one option first: it cannot be הקב"ה who was unsure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the uncertainty was משה's. So the גמרא first removes the possibility that הקב"ה said 'about.' הקב"ה knows everything exactly, so the word cannot reflect any doubt on His part.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces an idea the גמרא is about to reject
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: What does "about midnight" mean?
If you say that He said to him
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said "about midnight"
is there any doubt before Heaven?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the פסוק used as proof in Step 34
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who used the word 'about,' and whose uncertainty does it show?

steps.title: משה was the one who was unsure
steps.stepSummary: הקב"ה told משה 'at midnight,' but משה told פרעה 'about midnight.' So the uncertainty was משה's, which makes the question on דוד even stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, הקב"ה told him 'at midnight,' and משה came and said 'about midnight.' So משה was unsure, and דוד knew?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: הקב"ה said the exact time, and משה changed it to 'about.' This confirms that משה did not know the exact moment, and the challenge on דוד stands even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the proof is secure. The word 'about' came from משה, so משה himself was unsure of the exact moment. If even משה did not know it, it is very hard to say that דוד knew it. Step 37 answers this challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the one-letter difference: בַּחֲצוֹת means 'at midnight' (exact), while כַּחֲצוֹת means 'about midnight' (an estimate). The whole proof depends on it.

phrases.english: Rather: He said to him (tomorrow)
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. If you keep it, read: 'tomorrow, at midnight, like now.'

phrases.english: "at midnight" (like now),
and he came and said "about midnight",
so apparently he was unsure,
and David knew?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 35 and uses the answer to restate the challenge of Step 34 more strongly
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקב"ה said 'at midnight' exactly. משה changed it to 'about midnight' because he was unsure of the exact moment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next stage of the סוגיא, which must explain how דוד could know midnight when משה could not.

steps.title: דוד had a sign: the כנור that played at midnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that דוד had a sign. A כנור above his bed played by itself when the north wind blew at midnight. That told him the exact moment, and he got up and learned תורה until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד had a sign. As רב אחא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: a כנור (harp) hung above דוד's bed. When midnight came, the north wind blew on it and it played by itself. Right away דוד would get up and learn Torah until dawn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 34: דוד did not have to figure out midnight on his own, because a sign told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה said 'about midnight' because a person cannot sense the exact moment by himself. דוד's knowledge came from an outside signal, the north wind playing his כנור exactly at midnight. So the question on דוד falls away, and the פסוק 'חצות לילה אקום' can mean the exact moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Midnight, the exact middle of the night
Dawn, the first light of morning

steps.whatToRemember: דוד knew the exact moment of midnight because of an outside sign, his כנור playing in the north wind, and not through his own reckoning.

phrases.english: David had a sign,
as Rav Acha bar Bizna said,
Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּנּוֹר הָיָה תָּלוּי לְמַעְלָה מִמִּטָּתוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד,
phrases.english: a harp hung above David's bed,
and once midnight arrived,
the north wind would come and blow on it
and it would play by itself.
Immediately he would get up and learn Torah
until dawn came up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the strengthened question from Steps 34 and 36 about how דוד could know the exact moment of midnight.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation: an outside sign gave דוד the exact time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since even משה did not know the exact moment of midnight, דוד could not have known it either.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד had a signal, the כנור played by the north wind at midnight, so he knew the exact moment.

steps.title: At dawn the חכמים ask דוד for the people's livelihood
steps.stepSummary: The story goes on. At dawn the חכמי ישראל came to דוד and told him the people needed a livelihood. דוד answered that they should support one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: When dawn came, the חכמי ישראל came in to him. They said: Our master the king, your people ישראל need a livelihood. He told them: Go and support yourselves from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps telling the story of דוד's night and morning. Now it describes the first meeting of the day with the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part does not help answer the midnight question. It continues the אגדה about דוד's daily schedule. דוד's first answer is to share within the nation: let those who have more help those who have less.

phrases.english: Once dawn came up,
the Sages of Israel came in to him.
They said to him: Our master the king,
your people Israel need a livelihood.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לְכוּ וְהִתְפַּרְנְסוּ זֶה מִזֶּה.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go and support yourselves from one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר נִכְנְסוּ חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶצְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי שמעון חסידא from where דוד learned until dawn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At dawn the חכמים asked דוד for the people's livelihood, and he told them to support one another.

steps.title: The חכמים say that is not enough, and דוד sends them to war
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer with two comparisons: one handful cannot fill a lion, and a pit cannot fill up from the rain falling into its own opening. So the nation cannot live off itself. דוד then tells them to go out with the troops.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A handful does not satisfy a lion, and a pit is not filled from its own opening. He said to them: Go and stretch out your hands with the troops, meaning go out to war.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on דוד's first answer, and דוד gives a second answer: go out to battle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both comparisons make the same point. A closed system cannot feed itself, so help has to come from outside. Because of that, דוד sends the people to war to gain land and resources.

keyTerms.meaning: Its opening or rim (of a pit)
A troop or band of soldiers

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין הַקּוֹמֶץ מַשְׂבִּיעַ אֶת הָאֲרִי,
phrases.english: They said to him: A handful does not satisfy a lion,
and a pit is not filled from its own opening.
phrases.notes: A pit can't fill up just from the rain that drops straight into its mouth. Water has to be brought in from outside.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לְכוּ וּפִשְׁטוּ יְדֵיכֶם בִּגְדוּד.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go and stretch out your hands with the troops.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין הַקּוֹמֶץ מַשְׂבִּיעַ אֶת הָאֲרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים reject דוד's suggestion from Step 38, and דוד answers with a new plan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nation cannot live only off its own resources, so דוד sends them out to war.

steps.title: Before going to war: אחיתופל, the סנהדרין, and the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: Right away they took advice from אחיתופל, consulted the סנהדרין, and asked the אורים ותומים before going out to war.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away they take advice from אחיתופל, consult with the סנהדרין, and ask the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by listing the three things that were done before going out to war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going to war was not done on the king's word alone. They asked three different sources: a wise adviser (אחיתופל), the court (סנהדרין), and the כהן גדול's breastplate (אורים ותומים). This list sets up רב יוסף's question in the next step about which פסוק it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול's breastplate, used to ask Heaven questions

phrases.english: Right away they take advice from Ahitophel,
and consult with the Sanhedrin,
and ask the Urim VeTummim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what was done after דוד ordered them to war in Step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before war they consulted אחיתופל, the סנהדרין, and the אורים ותומים.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings the verse behind the story
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks which פסוק this story is based on. He quotes the פסוק listing אחיתופל, בניהו בן יהוידע, אביתר, and יואב the general.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the פסוק? As it is written: 'And after אחיתופל was בניהו בן יהוידע and אביתר, and the king's general was יואב.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a source in תנ"ך for the story just told, and quotes the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists דוד's advisers in a fixed order. רב יוסף sees that order as matching the steps of the story: an adviser, then the court, then the אורים ותומים, then the general. The next lines begin to match each name to its role.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse (that this is based on)?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?
As it is written: 'And after Ahitophel
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 27:34

phrases.english: was Benayahu son of Yehoyada and Evyatar,
and the king's general was Yoav.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for the order of consultation described in Step 40.
steps.raayaObject: The story that before war they consulted an adviser, the סנהדרין, and the אורים ותומים
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 27:34, which lists אחיתופל, בניהו בן יהוידע, אביתר, and יואב in order

steps.title: אחיתופל is the adviser
steps.stepSummary: The first name in the פסוק, אחיתופל, matches the adviser in the story. A פסוק in שמואל ב shows that his advice was treated like asking the word of God.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחיתופל is the adviser. And so it says: 'And the advice of אחיתופל that he gave in those days was as if a man asked the word of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts matching the names in רב יוסף's פסוק to the roles in the story, beginning with אחיתופל as the adviser.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second פסוק proves that אחיתופל's job was to give advice, and that his advice was taken very seriously. So he fits the first step in the story: 'they take advice from אחיתופל.'

phrases.english: Ahitophel is the adviser,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וַעֲצַת אֲחִיתֹפֶל אֲשֶׁר יָעַץ
phrases.english: and so it says: 'And the advice of Ahitophel that he gave
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 16:23

phrases.english: in those days
was as if a man asked the word of God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the פסוק from Step 41 by identifying the first name in it.
steps.raayaObject: That אחיתופל in the פסוק stands for the adviser in the story
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 16:23, describing אחיתופל's advice as like asking the word of God
